subject: Helpshift
title: Helpshift Alternatives in 2026
description: Ten Helpshift alternatives for mobile game support desks, from AIHelp and Zendesk to Help Scout, Crisp and Freshdesk, with pricing where published.
intro: Helpshift calls itself the AI-native player engagement platform, with in-game support SDKs for mobile, PC and web and console support through QR codes and links; its home page names Zynga, Jam City, Rovio and Gameloft among its case studies. Mobile game teams look past it when price, team size or tooling does not line up. Here are ten alternatives, from a game-focused rival to general helpdesks that you wire into your game through a widget or API.
why_switch: Unpublished pricing: Helpshift's opened home page showed no prices, so teams compare against vendors that list figures.
Team size: a small studio may not need a platform aimed at large publishers and prefer a helpdesk with a free plan.
Channel mix: studios that support players on email, live chat and social may want a general helpdesk with those channels built in.
AI costs: some tools charge per resolution or per outcome, which changes the math for high-volume games.
Data location: a European studio may prefer a vendor that states it is built in Europe.

picks.name: AIHelp
picks.pricing: Free trial offered; pricing is on a separate page that was not opened.
picks.note: AIHelp is the closest in kind: an in-app and web customer support platform with AI chatbots, in-app messaging, push notifications and web chat, delivered as a mobile SDK. Its home page claims 30K clients and 800M+ monthly active users, which are vendor claims. You gain a comparable setup with a free trial; you give up the case-study names Helpshift shows, and you must open the pricing page yourself.

sources.fact: AIHelp's home page lists in-app messaging, AI chat bots, push notifications and web chat.
AIHelp's home page offers a 'Get Free Trial' and links to a separate Pricing page.

picks.name: Zendesk
picks.pricing: 14-day free trial, no card; eligible startups up to 2 years free; plan prices not on the page.
picks.note: Zendesk's home page describes self-learning AI agents and channels including email, messaging, live chat, phone, social media and help centers. That suits a publisher with a large player base and a support team in several time zones. You gain channel depth and a startup program; you give up game-specific SDK focus, and the opened page did not list plan prices.

sources.fact: Zendesk's home page lists channels including email, messaging, live chat, phone, social media and help centers.
Zendesk's home page says eligible startups can get up to 2 years of Zendesk free.

picks.name: Freshdesk
picks.pricing: Plans at $19 and $55 per agent per month billed annually; Freddy AI Copilot add-on at $29 per agent per month.
picks.note: Freshdesk from Freshworks offers omnichannel ticketing and automated workflows with prices posted: $19 and $55 per agent per month billed annually. A studio can see its cost per support agent in advance. You gain price transparency; you give up an in-game SDK built for mobile players, so players will reach you through a web form or widget you embed.

sources.fact: The Freshdesk pricing page lists $19 and $55 per agent per month, billed annually, and offers a Try it free option.
The Freshdesk pricing page lists Freddy AI Copilot at $29 per agent per month as an add-on.

picks.name: Intercom
picks.best_for: Automated resolution with an AI agent
picks.pricing: Helpdesk with Fin AI Agent at $19 per seat per month plus $0.99 per outcome; 14-day free trial.
picks.note: Intercom pairs a helpdesk with its Fin AI Agent and bills $0.99 per outcome on top of $19 per seat per month, with spending limits you can set. High-volume games with repetitive questions about purchases or accounts may like that model. You gain automation; you give up flat predictability, since cost rises with resolved conversations. No free plan is mentioned.

sources.fact: Intercom's home page lists the helpdesk with Fin AI Agent at $19 per seat per month plus $0.99 per outcome.
Intercom's home page offers a 14 day free trial with no credit card required and mentions no free plan.

picks.name: Help Scout
picks.best_for: Small studios wanting a shared inbox
picks.pricing: Paid plans at $25, $45 and $75 per user per month; free plan for 5 users, 1 Inbox and 1 Docs site.
picks.note: Help Scout gives a shared inbox, AI assistance, workflow automation and a help docs product, with a free plan for 5 users. A five-person indie studio can run player email support there at no cost. You gain a gentle start and a docs site; you give up in-game messaging, and AI resolutions are billed at $0.75 each if you add that feature.

sources.fact: The Help Scout pricing page lists paid plans at $25, $45 and $75 per user per month, and a free plan with 5 users, 1 Inbox and 1 Docs site.
Help Scout is an AI-driven support platform with a shared Inbox, Copilot AI assistance, Envoy workflow automation and Signal insights, per its homepage.

picks.name: Kustomer
picks.pricing: Not on page; a Pricing link exists without prices.
picks.note: Kustomer describes an AI-native platform that combines omnichannel support, CRM, workflows and analytics, with AI features named Concierge, Envoy, Architect, Data Explorer and AI QA. Its listed customers are consumer brands such as sweetgreen and Turo, not games. You gain a CRM view of each customer; you give up game-specific features and published pricing.

sources.fact: Kustomer's home page lists AI features including Concierge, Envoy, Architect, Data Explorer and AI QA.
Kustomer's home page links to a Pricing page but shows no prices or free plan.

picks.name: Zoho Desk
picks.best_for: Low-cost helpdesk with a free tier
picks.pricing: Express from INR 420, Professional INR 1,400, Enterprise INR 2,400 per user per month billed annually; Free plan listed.
picks.note: Zoho Desk brings conversations from every channel into one workspace and lists a Free plan plus free trials on each paid plan. The opened pricing page showed rupee figures, so convert them for your own billing currency before you compare. You gain a low entry cost; you give up a game-oriented SDK and need to confirm that currency and invoicing suit your accounting.

sources.fact: The Zoho Desk pricing page lists per-user per-month plans billed annually, with Express from INR 420, Professional from INR 1,400 and Enterprise from INR 2,400.
The Zoho Desk pricing page offers a Free plan, free trials for each paid plan, and a quote request option.

picks.name: Crisp
picks.pricing: Homepage links to a pricing page; no amounts shown.
picks.note: Crisp is an AI customer support platform with a chat widget, shared inbox, knowledge base and support CRM, and its homepage says it is built from France and made in Europe; the copyright names Crisp IM SAS. European studios with data location concerns may start here. You gain a light chat-first tool; you give up an in-game SDK, and prices are only on the pricing page.

sources.fact: The homepage says Crisp is built from France and made in Europe.
The homepage describes Crisp as an AI customer support platform.

picks.name: Gladly
picks.pricing: Not published; demo or contact sales.
picks.note: Gladly positions itself as an agentic commerce platform bringing AI shopping assistance and support to brands' own websites. For a game with a large web shop it could handle pre-purchase questions. You gain commerce focus; you give up an in-game support flow, and you must go through a demo to learn anything about price.

sources.fact: Gladly brings agentic commerce to a brand's website for ecommerce support, with an AI assistant that answers shopper questions.
The Gladly site does not publish prices and offers a Get a demo button and a Contact sales page.

picks.name: LiveChat
picks.best_for: Live chat on a game website
picks.pricing: Pricing starts from $19 per user per month, per the homepage.
picks.note: LiveChat, now sold as Text by LiveChat, combines AI and human agents in live chat for websites, with pricing from $19 per user per month. It fits a studio selling through its own site or running a launcher landing page. You gain quick chat setup; you give up ticketing depth and in-game integration, and the pricing page itself was not opened.

sources.fact: The homepage states pricing starts from $19 per user per month.
The homepage describes Text by LiveChat as live chat software for websites that combines AI and human agents.

how_to_pick: Check where your players ask for help. If it is inside the game, AIHelp is the like-for-like test, since the others expect players to reach you through a web page or an embedded widget. If it is email, Help Scout (free for 5 users), Freshdesk ($19 and $55 per agent) and Zoho Desk keep cost visible. If a bot should absorb repetitive tickets, price Intercom's per-outcome fee against your monthly volume. Crisp is the pick when a European vendor matters. Our [player support ranking](/software/best-player-support-software-for-games) adds more detail.

faqs.q: Which alternative has an in-game SDK like Helpshift?
faqs.a: AIHelp is the one on this list that describes itself as an in-app and web support platform offered as a mobile SDK. The general helpdesks reach players through email, widgets and web chat, so you would embed a link or web view from the game.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to start?
faqs.a: Help Scout offers a free plan for 5 users, 1 Inbox and 1 Docs site, and Zoho Desk lists a Free plan. For paid use, Freshdesk lists $19 and $55 per agent per month billed annually and LiveChat says from $19 per user per month.

faqs.q: How does AI pricing differ between tools?
faqs.a: Intercom charges $0.99 per outcome on top of seat fees, Help Scout lists $0.75 per resolution for its AI add-on, and Freshdesk lists Freddy AI Copilot at $29 per agent per month. Per-resolution models scale with volume, per-agent add-ons scale with headcount.
Crisp says on its homepage that it is built from France and made in Europe, and names Crisp IM SAS in its copyright. Whether that satisfies your data rules is for your legal team to confirm.

faqs.q: Do these tools suit console or PC games?
faqs.a: General helpdesks work on any platform because the player contacts you by web or email. Helpshift's own page mentions PC and web SDKs and QR codes for console, so if you rely on that, test how your chosen tool handles the same cases.
